A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes the published path of a `files` entry. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` is served at its path relative to `root`, unless a `files` map entry states its served path. Claude sends it with every such publish, set to the folder that holds the Artifact's files at their served paths.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

"""(e) End-to-end run of the REAL SkellyCam camera-group stack with synthetic 60 fps cameras.

What is real (unmodified SkellyCam HEAD 23ccbf20 code):
  WorkerRegistry(WorkerMode.PROCESS) + heartbeat, CameraGroupManager.create_and_start_camera_group,
  CameraGroup/CameraManager/CameraWorker/ManagedProcess (spawned camera processes), opencv_camera_worker_method,
  setup_opencv_camera_loop, run_opencv_camera_loop (lockstep orchestrator, opencv_get_frame incl. putText overlay,
  put_frame(overwrite=True), handle_video_recording -> VideoRecorder.record_frame, check_framerate_reset),
  start_recording_all_groups / stop_recording_all_groups (pause, RecordingInfoMessage, RecordingFinalizer incl.
  validate_recording), and the UI read path CameraGroupManager.get_latest_frontend_payloads (called the way
  WebsocketServer._frontend_image_relay calls it: await_10ms, then build, instant ack).

What is substituted (benchmark-process-only monkeypatch, applied at import of this script, which spawn re-imports
as __mp_main__ in every camera child before the worker runs):
  create_cv2_video_capture -> returns FakeCapture(cv2.VideoCapture subclass). FakeCapture models a free-running
  sensor at SENSOR_FPS with "latest frame wins" (CAP_PROP_BUFFERSIZE=1-like) semantics: grab() blocks until the next
  sensor tick if the loop is early; if the loop is late, the skipped ticks are counted as sensor frames the loop
  never grabbed. retrieve(image=buf):
     mjpeg  : cv2.imdecode(pre-encoded JPEG q90 of the synthetic frame) then np.copyto(buf)  (decode CPU cost; adds one
              memcpy that an in-place backend decode might not have)
     memcpy : np.copyto(buf, synthetic frame)  (lower bound: no decode cost)
  This assumption about DSHOW buffering is an assumption (no real camera used), see README limitations.
Also instrumented (parent only): RecordingFinalizer.create is wrapped to keep a copy of the per-frame metadata.

Run:  cd C:\\Users\\Dom\\GitHub\\freemocap\\skellycam && .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe benchmarks\\frame_pipeline\\baseline\\bench_e_e2e.py [size] [mjpeg|memcpy] [ui|noui] [record_s]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import multiprocessing.queues  # noqa: F401  workaround for skellycam type_overloads.py L23 (see README)
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import cv2  # noqa: E402
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

N_CAMS = int(os.environ.get("BENCH_E2E_NCAMS", "5"))
SENSOR_FPS = float(os.environ.get("BENCH_SENSOR_FPS", "60"))
RETRIEVE_MODE = os.environ.get("BENCH_E2E_RETRIEVE", "mjpeg")
CAP_LOG_DIR = os.environ.get("BENCH_E2E_CAPLOG", "")


class FakeCapture(cv2.VideoCapture):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        import bench_common as bc
        self.cam = config.camera_id
        self.h, self.w = config.resolution.height, config.resolution.width
        self.period = int(1e9 / SENSOR_FPS)
        rng = np.random.default_rng(int(config.camera_index))
        self.t0 = time.perf_counter_ns() + int(rng.integers(0, self.period))  # free-running, random phase
        self.frames = bc.synthetic_frames(self.h, self.w, n=30, seed=int(config.camera_index), noise=8)
        self.jpegs = [cv2.imencode(".jpg", f, [int(cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY), 90])[1] for f in self.frames]
        self.last_tick = -1
        self.cur = 0
        self.opened = True
        self.grab_log = []  # (tick, tick_time_ns, grab_return_ns)
        self.skipped_ticks_during_grabs = 0
        self.reads = 0
        self.created_ns = time.perf_counter_ns()

    def _next_tick(self):
        now = time.perf_counter_ns()
        tick = (now - self.t0) // self.period
        if tick <= self.last_tick:
            tick = self.last_tick + 1
            target = self.t0 + tick * self.period
            while True:
                rem = target - time.perf_counter_ns()
                if rem <= 0:
                    break
                if rem > 2_000_000:
                    time.sleep((rem - 1_500_000) / 1e9)
            skipped = 0
        else:
            skipped = tick - self.last_tick - 1
        self.last_tick = tick
        self.cur = tick
        return tick, skipped

    def isOpened(self):
        return self.opened

    def grab(self):
        tick, skipped = self._next_tick()
        if self.grab_log:
            self.skipped_ticks_during_grabs += skipped
        self.grab_log.append((int(tick), int(self.t0 + tick * self.period), time.perf_counter_ns()))
        return True

    def retrieve(self, image=None, flag=None):
        k = self.cur % len(self.frames)
        if RETRIEVE_MODE == "mjpeg":
            dec = cv2.imdecode(self.jpegs[k], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        else:
            dec = self.frames[k]
        if image is None:
            return True, dec.copy()
        np.copyto(image, dec)
        return True, image

    def read(self, image=None):
        self._next_tick()
        self.reads += 1
        return self.retrieve(image)

    def get(self, prop):
        return 0.0

    def set(self, prop, value):
        return True

    def release(self):
        if self.opened and CAP_LOG_DIR:
            p = Path(CAP_LOG_DIR) / f"cap_{self.cam}_{self.created_ns}.json"
            p.write_text(json.dumps(dict(camera_id=self.cam, period_ns=self.period, t0=self.t0, reads=self.reads,
                                         skipped_ticks_during_grabs=self.skipped_ticks_during_grabs,
                                         grab_log=self.grab_log)))
        self.opened = False

CAPTURED_METADATA = {}


def _wrap_finalizer():
    from skellycam.core.recorders.recording_finalizer import RecordingFinalizer
    orig = RecordingFinalizer.create.__func__

    def create(cls, recording_info, camera_configs, frame_metadatas_by_camera):
        CAPTURED_METADATA.update({k: [np.copy(m) for m in v] for k, v in frame_metadatas_by_camera.items()})
        return orig(cls, recording_info=recording_info, camera_configs=camera_configs,
                    frame_metadatas_by_camera=frame_metadatas_by_camera)
    RecordingFinalizer.create = classmethod(create)


def _meta_arrays(mlist):
    md = np.concatenate([np.asarray(m).reshape(-1) for m in mlist])
    ts = md["timestamps"]
    return md["frame_number"].astype(np.int64), {n: ts[n].astype(np.int64) for n in ts.dtype.names}


async def run(size_name, ui, record_s, warmup_s=5.0):
    import asyncio
    import multiprocessing as mp
    import shutil
    import psutil
    import bench_common as bc
    from skellycam.core.camera_group.camera_group_manager import CameraGroupManager
    from skellycam.core.ipc.process_management.managed_worker import WorkerMode
    from skellycam.core.ipc.process_management.worker_registry import WorkerRegistry
    from skellycam.core.recorders.videos.recording_info import RecordingInfo
    from skellycam.utilities.wait_functions import await_10ms

    _wrap_finalizer()
    h, w = bc.SIZES[size_name]
    pc = time.perf_counter_ns
    kill = mp.Value("b", False)
    reg = WorkerRegistry(global_kill_flag=kill, worker_mode=WorkerMode.PROCESS)
    reg.start_heartbeat()
    cgm = CameraGroupManager(global_kill_flag=kill, worker_registry=reg)
    configs = {str(i): bc.make_config(i, h, w, framerate=SENSOR_FPS) for i in range(N_CAMS)}
    t_setup = time.perf_counter()
    group = await cgm.create_and_start_camera_group(configs)
    while not group.cameras.all_ready:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    setup_s = time.perf_counter() - t_setup

    ui_stats = dict(build_ns=[], fns=[], age_ns=[], sizes=[], errors=[], t=[])
    running = {"ui": True}

    async def ui_task():
        last = -1
        while running["ui"]:
            await await_10ms()
            a = pc()
            try:
                payloads = cgm.get_latest_frontend_payloads(if_newer_than=last, display_image_sizes=None)
            except Exception as e:  # the real relay would set global_kill_flag here
                ui_stats["errors"].append(repr(e))
                continue
            b = pc()
            for gid, (fn, mfts, payload) in payloads.items():
                ui_stats["build_ns"].append(b - a); ui_stats["fns"].append(int(fn)); ui_stats["t"].append(b)
                ui_stats["age_ns"].append(b - float(mfts)); ui_stats["sizes"].append(len(payload))
                last = int(fn)

    me = psutil.Process()
    cpu_samples = []

    async def cpu_task():
        procs = {}
        while running["ui"]:
            kids = me.children(recursive=True)
            for k in kids:
                if k.pid not in procs:
                    procs[k.pid] = k
                    try:
                        k.cpu_percent(None)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
            me.cpu_percent(None) if not cpu_samples else None
            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
            row = {"t": time.perf_counter(), "system": psutil.cpu_percent(None), "main": me.cpu_percent(None)}
            for pid, k in procs.items():
                try:
                    row[str(pid)] = k.cpu_percent(None)
                except Exception:
                    pass
            cpu_samples.append(row)

    psutil.cpu_percent(None)
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(cpu_task())]
    if ui:
        tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(ui_task()))
    await asyncio.sleep(warmup_s)
    rec_name = f"e2e_{size_name}_{RETRIEVE_MODE}_{'ui' if ui else 'noui'}_{int(time.time())}"
    info = RecordingInfo(recording_name=rec_name, recording_directory=str(bc.SCRATCH_TMP))
    t_rec0 = pc()
    await cgm.start_recording_all_groups(recording_info=info)
    t_rec1 = pc()
    await asyncio.sleep(record_s)
    t_stop0 = pc()
    stop_error = None
    stats_str = None
    try:
        res = await cgm.stop_recording_all_groups()
        stats_str = str(res[0][1]) if res else None
    except Exception as e:
        stop_error = repr(e)
    t_stop1 = pc()
    running["ui"] = False
    await asyncio.sleep(1.2)
    for t in tasks:
        t.cancel()
    await cgm.close_all_camera_groups()
    reg.shutdown_all()
    return dict(setup_s=setup_s, t_rec_start_call=(t_rec0, t_rec1), t_stop_call=(t_stop0, t_stop1),
                stop_error=stop_error, finalizer_stats=stats_str, ui=ui_stats, cpu_samples=cpu_samples,
                recording_folder=info.full_recording_path, kill_flag=bool(kill.value))


def analyse(size_name, ui, record_s, raw):
    import bench_common as bc
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
    caplogs = {}
    for p in Path(CAP_LOG_DIR).glob("cap_*.json"):
        d = json.loads(p.read_text())
        caplogs.setdefault(d["camera_id"], []).append(d)
    per_cam = {}
    grab_by_cam = {}
    for cam, mlist in sorted(CAPTURED_METADATA.items()):
        fn, ts = _meta_arrays(mlist)
        logs = caplogs.get(cam, [])
        log = max(logs, key=lambda d: len(d["grab_log"]))["grab_log"] if logs else []
        log = np.asarray(log, dtype=np.int64) if log else np.zeros((0, 3), np.int64)
        sel = fn[(fn >= 0) & (fn < len(log))]
        ticks = log[sel, 0] if len(sel) else np.array([])
        tick_t = log[sel, 1] if len(sel) else np.array([])
        sensor_frames = int(ticks[-1] - ticks[0] + 1) if len(ticks) else 0
        grab = ts["pre_frame_grab_ns"]
        grab_by_cam[cam] = dict(zip(fn.tolist(), grab.tolist()))
        dt = np.diff(grab)
        rec_done = ts["post_frame_record_ns"]
        per_cam[cam] = dict(
            recorded_frames=int(len(fn)), first_fn=int(fn[0]), last_fn=int(fn[-1]),
            consecutive=bool(np.all(np.diff(fn) == 1)),
            sensor_frames_during_recording=sensor_frames,
            sensor_frames_never_grabbed=int(sensor_frames - len(fn)) if sensor_frames else None,
            achieved_fps=float((len(fn) - 1) / ((grab[-1] - grab[0]) / 1e9)),
            grab_interval=bc.stats_ms(dt),
            retrieve=bc.stats_ms(ts["post_frame_retrieve_ns"] - ts["pre_frame_retrieve_ns"]),
            put_frame=bc.stats_ms(ts["post_copy_to_camera_shm_ns"] - ts["pre_copy_to_camera_shm_ns"]),
            record_frame_write=bc.stats_ms(ts["post_frame_record_ns"] - ts["pre_frame_record_ns"]),
            grab_to_written=bc.stats_ms(rec_done - ts["post_frame_grab_ns"]),
            sensor_tick_to_written=bc.stats_ms(rec_done[:len(tick_t)] - tick_t) if len(tick_t) else None,
        )
    # cross-camera grab spread per frame number
    common = set.intersection(*[set(d) for d in grab_by_cam.values()]) if grab_by_cam else set()
    spread = [max(grab_by_cam[c][f] for c in grab_by_cam) - min(grab_by_cam[c][f] for c in grab_by_cam) for f in sorted(common)]
    # count frames actually in files
    vids = sorted(Path(raw["recording_folder"]).rglob("*.mp4")) + sorted(Path(raw["recording_folder"]).rglob("*.avi"))

    def count(path):
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(path))
        n = 0
        while cap.grab():
            n += 1
        prop = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT))
        cap.release()
        return dict(file=path.name, bytes=path.stat().st_size, decoded_frames=n, prop_frame_count=prop)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(5) as ex:
        files = list(ex.map(count, vids))
    total_bytes = sum(f.stat().st_size for f in Path(raw["recording_folder"]).rglob("*") if f.is_file())
    u = raw["ui"]
    ui_summary = None
    if ui and u["fns"]:
        el = (u["t"][-1] - u["t"][0]) / 1e9
        ui_summary = dict(payloads=len(u["fns"]), payload_fps=len(u["fns"]) / el, distinct_fps=len(set(u["fns"])) / el,
                          build=bc.stats_ms(u["build_ns"]), age_when_ready=bc.stats_ms(u["age_ns"]),
                          payload_bytes_median=float(np.median(u["sizes"])), errors=u["errors"][:5], n_errors=len(u["errors"]))
    # CPU summary (mean over samples taken during the recording window)
    t0r = raw["t_rec_start_call"][1] / 1e9
    t1r = raw["t_stop_call"][0] / 1e9
    win = [s for s in raw["cpu_samples"] if t0r + 1 <= s["t"] <= t1r]
    cpu = None
    if win:
        keys = [k for k in win[0] if k not in ("t",)]
        cpu = {k: float(np.mean([s.get(k, 0) for s in win])) for k in keys}
        cpu["sum_child_processes"] = float(sum(v for k, v in cpu.items() if k not in ("system", "main")))
    return dict(size=size_name, retrieve_mode=RETRIEVE_MODE, ui=ui, record_s=record_s, n_cams=N_CAMS, sensor_fps=SENSOR_FPS,
                setup_s=raw["setup_s"], start_recording_call_s=(raw["t_rec_start_call"][1] - raw["t_rec_start_call"][0]) / 1e9,
                stop_recording_call_s=(raw["t_stop_call"][1] - raw["t_stop_call"][0]) / 1e9,
                stop_error=raw["stop_error"], kill_flag_set=raw["kill_flag"], finalizer_stats=raw["finalizer_stats"],
                per_camera=per_cam, cross_camera_grab_spread=bc.stats_ms(spread), files=files,
                recording_total_bytes=total_bytes, ui_summary=ui_summary, cpu_pct_mean_during_recording=cpu,
                capture_logs={c: [dict(reads=d["reads"], skipped=d["skipped_ticks_during_grabs"], grabs=len(d["grab_log"])) for d in v]
                              for c, v in caplogs.items()})


def main():
    import asyncio
    import shutil
    import bench_common as bc
    size_name = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "1080p"

    print("RESULT", json.dumps({k: res[k] for k in ("size", "retrieve_mode", "ui", "stop_error", "kill_flag_set")}))
    for cam, d in res["per_camera"].items():
        print("CAM", cam, f"fps={d['achieved_fps']:.2f} rec={d['recorded_frames']} sensor={d['sensor_frames_during_recording']} "

def make_config(cam_idx: int, height: int, width: int, framerate: float = 60.0, **kw):

    from skellycam.core.camera.config.image_resolution import ImageResolution

def make_frame_recarray(config, timebase_mapping=None) -> np.recarray:
    """Same construction as skellycam create_initial_frame_rec_array (which needs a CameraGroupIPC)."""
    from skellycam.core.types.frame_dtype_factories import create_frame_dtype
    from skellycam.core.timestamps.timebase_mapping import TimebaseMapping
    tbm = timebase_mapping or TimebaseMapping()
    fr = np.recarray(1, dtype=create_frame_dtype(config))
    fr.frame_metadata.camera_info[0] = config.to_frame_camera_info()
    fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = -1
    fr.frame_metadata.timebase_mapping[0] = tbm.to_numpy_record_array()
    fr.image[0] = np.zeros((config.resolution.height, config.resolution.width, 3), np.uint8) + config.camera_index
    return fr


def synthetic_frames(height: int, width: int, n: int = 60, seed: int = 0, noise: int = 8) -> np.ndarray:
    """n distinct BGR frames: moving diagonal gradient + moving box + uniform noise (+-noise).
    Moderately compressible, closer to a real scene than pure noise or a flat image."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[0:height, 0:width]
    out = np.empty((n, height, width, 3), np.uint8)
    for i in range(n):
        g = ((xx + yy + 8 * i) % 256).astype(np.int16)
        img = np.stack([g, (g * 2) % 256, 255 - g], axis=-1)
        bx = (i * width // n) % (width - width // 6)
        img[height // 3: height // 3 + height // 4, bx: bx + width // 6] = (40, 200, 90)
        if noise:
            img = img + rng.integers(-noise, noise + 1, img.shape, dtype=np.int16)
        out[i] = np.clip(img, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return out


def stats_ms(samples_ns) -> dict:
    a = np.asarray(samples_ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    if a.size == 0:
        return {"n": 0}
    return {"n": int(a.size), "median_ms": float(np.median(a)), "mean_ms": float(a.mean()),
            "p99_ms": float(np.percentile(a, 99)), "min_ms": float(a.min()), "max_ms": float(a.max())}

# Baseline benchmarks: the current SkellyCam frame pipeline (HEAD 23ccbf20)

These benchmarks measure the SkellyCam pipeline as it is at `23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d`, using the real
SkellyCam classes from the SkellyCam venv (`C:\Users\Dom\GitHub\freemocap\skellycam\.venv`). No SkellyCam source file is
modified. Where a benchmark wraps or substitutes something, it does so inside the benchmark process only, and the script
docstring says what it changes. Every multi-process benchmark uses `multiprocessing` spawn, which is what SkellyCam uses
on Windows.

Reference sizes: 1280x720 and 1920x1080, BGR uint8 x3. That is SkellyCam's native layout: a `frame_metadata` record of
632 B followed by an HxWx3 image, giving 2,765,432 B per record at 720p and 6,221,432 B at 1080p
(`results/f_copies.md`). Ring lengths are 388 slots at 720p and 172 at 1080p (`results/a_write.json`, `ring_len`).

Summary: i7-14700K (20 cores / 28 threads), 64 GB DDR5 running at 4000 MT/s, WD_BLACK SN850X 4 TB NVMe, Windows 11 Home

av 18.0.0, psutil 7.2.2, polars 1.43.0 (now present in the SkellyCam venv), uvicorn 0.51.0. No C/C++ code was compiled
for these benchmarks.

## Results (headline numbers; every number is in the named file)

### (a) Write: `put_frame` (`results/a_write.md`)
Each spawned writer process writes as fast as it can for 10 s, after one full first lap of the ring.

| size | N | production put_frame median / worst p99 (ms) | per-camera max fps (slowest camera) | single-copy reference median (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 720p | 1 | 0.629 / 0.827 | 1539 | 0.089 |
| 720p | 5 | 1.167 / 1.891 | 819 | 0.263 |
| 1080p | 1 | 1.352 / 1.825 | 717 | 0.174 |
| 1080p | 5 | 2.936 / 4.412 | 337 | 0.644 |

The first lap through fresh pages has a median of 2.9 to 3.2 ms at 1080p. The writer never caps throughput at 60 fps: even 5x1080p
unthrottled reaches 337 fps per camera. Throughput saturates at about 10.6 to 11.5 GB/s aggregate for production and
about 38 to 50 GB/s for a single copy, which means production achieves about 4 to 7x less useful bandwidth than one copy
would. When the machine is loaded the way the e2e run loads it (5 x encode + decode + UI, 60 fps), `put_frame` is slower than when run
alone: 1080p median 2.3 to 2.9 ms (memcpy mode) and 4.1 to 4.2 ms (mjpeg mode), against 1.35 ms isolated
(`results/e_e2e_summary.md`, column put_frame).

### (b) Read styles (`results/b_read.md`, 5 x 60 fps writers; "cold" means the first read after a new frame is published)
1080p cold medians: `get_data_by_index` (reused buffer) 0.50 ms, `get_latest_data` (reused) 0.53 ms, `get_latest_data`
(allocating) 1.21 ms, `get_next_data` 0.56 ms, view only 0.03 ms. Multi-frame reads (5 cameras): `get_latest_multiframe` 2.42 ms,
`get_images_by_frame_number` 6.15 ms (it allocates five records on every call because `_frame_recarray_cache` is never filled),
5 views 0.06 ms. The 720p values are noisy: round medians vary 2 to 4x, as shown in the range column. There were no frame_number
mismatches in any style.

### (c) Record (`results/c_record.md`)
The default `writer_fourcc` X264 resolves to the **MSMF** backend in every process. All files contained exactly the number of frames
written (each file was decoded and counted).

| size | 5 cameras, paced at 60 fps for 20 s | record_frame median / p99 / max (ms) | summed process CPU (100 = 1 logical CPU) | release() |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 720p | 60.0 fps per camera, 0 writes over 16.7 ms | 0.97 / 2.36 / 4.22 | 380% (~74-84% per camera) | 0.08 s |
| 1080p | 60.0 fps per camera, 0 writes over 16.7 ms | 2.18 / 5.22 / 9.28 | **1169%** (~225-244% per camera) | 0.09-0.10 s |

When unthrottled, `write()` returns faster than the encoder finishes: `release()` then takes 1.8 to 2.2 s with 5 cameras and
5.3 to 6.5 s with 1 camera (`c_record.json` `release_s`). The "unthrottled fps" column therefore measures how fast `write()`
returns, not how fast frames are encoded. Derived from the same JSON (frames / (loop time + release time)), the encode
throughput is about 245 fps per camera at 5x720p, about 116 fps per camera at 5x1080p, about 613 fps for 1x720p and about
342 fps for 1x1080p. These are derived numbers, not separate measurements.

### (d) UI path (`results/d_ui.md`)
Relay-style loop: `await_10ms`, then build. The ack is instant because no browser is attached, so these are upper bounds on the
server-side UI work.

| size | path | payloads/s | shm copy median (ms) | resize+JPEG+pack median (ms) | total median / p99 (ms) | payload KB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 720p | SkellyCam UI (`get_latest_multiframe`) | 59.9 | 2.21 | 3.59 | 6.28 / 11.20 | 153 |
| 1080p | SkellyCam UI | 43.7 | 3.39 | 7.24 | 10.90 / 23.76 | 337 |
| 1080p | FreeMoCap UI (`get_images_by_frame_number`) | 37.9 | 7.29 | 8.07 | 15.43 / 27.82 | 337 |
| 1080p | SkellyCam UI, no sleep (maximum rate) | 70.7 (58.2 distinct) | 3.96 | 9.67 | 13.81 / 21.88 | 337 |

At 1080p the build cost alone (about 11 to 14 ms of the main event loop per payload) keeps the UI below 60 fps. In the full
e2e run the UI reached 34.8 to 41.0 payloads/s at 1080p and 55 to 60 at 720p (`e_e2e_summary.md`).

### (e) End-to-end, real stack (`results/e_e2e_summary.md`)
5 cameras, 60 fps sensors, 30 s recording, UI consumer on unless stated otherwise.

| config | achieved fps per camera | sensor frames never grabbed (sum of 5 cameras) | frames in files == frames recorded | sensor tick -> frame written median / p99 / max (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 720p, memcpy stand-in (2 runs) | 58.76 / 60.00 | 186 / 0 | yes / yes | 2.5/17.3/63.7 ; 2.1/3.6/9.1 |
| 720p, mjpeg stand-in | 59.99 | 0 | yes | 6.7 / 12.9 / 20.0 |
| 1080p, memcpy stand-in (2 runs) | 59.99 / 59.95 | 0 / 5 | yes / yes | ~5 / 9-15 / 23-30 |
| 1080p, mjpeg stand-in (2 runs) | **44.01 / 46.78** | **2398 / 1984** (about 25%) | yes / yes | 27 / 39 / 47 |
| 1080p, mjpeg stand-in, no UI | **46.11** | **2084** | yes | 27.0 / 39.8 / 45.3 |

Disk writes never lost a frame the loop had grabbed: every recorded frame number is consecutive, every file decodes to the
recorded count, and the real `RecordingFinalizer.validate_recording` passed in all runs (`stop_error: null`). Frames are lost
**before** the recorder sees them. When one lockstep iteration (retrieve, then putText, then `put_frame`, then `record_frame`) takes longer
than 16.7 ms on the slowest camera, the sensor's newer frame replaces the one that was never grabbed. At 1080p with an in-loop
MJPEG decode (retrieve median 11.2 to 12.3 ms under load, against 6.98 ms isolated in `g_decode_ref.md`), plus `put_frame` at
about 4.1 ms and `record_frame` at about 1.3 ms, the group interval rises to a median of about 21 to 22 ms. The SkellyCam frame numbers and
the finalizer's own statistics ("Mean Framerate: 44.52 Hz"; `finalizer_stats` in `e_e2e_1080p_mjpeg_ui.json`) still look
gap-free. Nothing in the ring itself was overwritten or dropped: the UI and recorder never lag the ring, and the recorder does not read the ring at all.
The 186 missed frames in the first 720p memcpy run come from group-wide stalls (grab interval max 89 to 130 ms on every
camera at once) during a period when other workloads were running on the machine (see Limitations). A repeat run had 0.

"""(a) Ring-buffer WRITE benchmark using the real SkellyCam shared-memory classes.

Topology (mirrors SkellyCam): the parent creates CameraGroupSharedMemory.create(..., read_only=True)
(as CameraGroup.start does), and each camera gets its own *spawned* writer process that attaches with
CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer.recreate(dto, read_only=False) and calls put_frame(frame_rec_array,
overwrite=True) exactly like opencv_camera_loop.py L96.

Per config: every writer first does one full lap of the ring (first-touch page faults, timed
separately), then all writers start together and write UNTHROTTLED for DURATION_S seconds, timing
every put_frame call. That gives max sustained put_frame rate per camera with N cameras in parallel.

mode "production": camera_shm.put_frame(...)                  (copy.copy + slot assignment)
mode "single_copy_reference": np.copyto(buffer[i:i+1], frame) + last_written_index.value = i
     (NOT SkellyCam code - a reference for what one copy into the same shm slot costs)

Run:  cd C:\\Users\\Dom\\GitHub\\freemocap\\skellycam && .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe benchmarks\\frame_pipeline\\baseline\\bench_a_write.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import multiprocessing as mp
import multiprocessing.queues  # noqa: F401  workaround: skellycam type_overloads.py L23 needs it before spawn-child unpickles a DTO (see README)
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

DURATION_S = 10.0


def writer_proc(cam_idx, h, w, dto, mode, ready_q, start_evt, result_q):
    import bench_common as bc
    from skellycam.core.ipc.shared_memory.camera_shared_memory_ring_buffer import CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer
    ring = CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer.recreate(dto=dto, read_only=False)
    cfg = bc.make_config(cam_idx, h, w)
    fr = bc.make_frame_recarray(cfg)
    L = ring.ring_buffer_length
    pc = time.perf_counter_ns

    def put_prod():
        ring.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)

    buf = ring.ring_shm.buffer

    def put_ref():
        i = ring.last_written_index.value + 1
        np.copyto(buf[i % L: i % L + 1], fr)
        ring.last_written_index.value = i

    put = put_prod if mode == "production" else put_ref
    first_lap = []
    for _ in range(L):
        fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] += 1
        t0 = pc(); put(); first_lap.append(pc() - t0)
    ready_q.put(cam_idx)
    start_evt.wait()
    lat = []
    t_start = pc()
    deadline = t_start + int(DURATION_S * 1e9)
    n = 0
    while True:
        fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] += 1
        t0 = pc(); put(); t1 = pc()
        lat.append(t1 - t0)
        n += 1
        if t1 >= deadline:
            break
    elapsed = (pc() - t_start) / 1e9
    # verify last slot content landed in shm
    last = ring.last_written_index.value
    ok = int(buf[last % L].frame_metadata.frame_number) == int(fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0])
    result_q.put(dict(cam=cam_idx, n=n, elapsed_s=elapsed, fps=n / elapsed, ring_len=L,
                      itemsize=int(fr.dtype.itemsize), first_lap=bc.stats_ms(first_lap),
                      steady=bc.stats_ms(lat), last_slot_verified=ok))
    ring.close()

"""P1 - camera-process write path: decode/capture + publish into shared memory, current vs prototypes.

N=5 spawned writer processes (multiprocessing spawn, like SkellyCam camera workers) run UNTHROTTLED for RUN_S seconds
after a warm-up, at 1280x720 and 1920x1080 BGR. Each iteration = "get the next camera frame into shm":

  variant                         what one iteration does                                        full-frame copies after decode
  cur_imdecode_putframe     [S]   cv2.imdecode(q90 JPEG) -> np.copyto(private recarray.image)     3 (copyto private, copy.copy, slot)
                                  -> REAL CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer.put_frame(overwrite=True)    (= baseline e2e mjpeg stand-in + put_frame)
  cur_memcpy_putframe       [S]   np.copyto(private, frame) -> REAL put_frame                     2 (+1 stand-in memcpy)
  cur_vcap_putframe         [S]   cv2.VideoCapture(MJPEG .avi, CAP_FFMPEG).grab()+retrieve(image=private) -> REAL put_frame   2
  p_imdecode_copyslot             cv2.imdecode -> np.copyto(SeqRing slot view) -> seq commit        1
  p_memcpy_slot                   np.copyto(slot view, frame) -> seq commit                          1 (the stand-in memcpy itself)
  p_vcap_into_slot                VideoCapture.grab()+retrieve(image=SeqRing slot view) -> commit   0 (decoder writes the slot)
  p_simplejpeg_into_slot    [B]   simplejpeg.decode_jpeg(buffer=slot view, colorspace=BGR) -> commit 0 (libjpeg-turbo writes the slot)

  [S] needs the SkellyCam venv (real SkellyCam classes);  [B] needs simplejpeg (bench venv).  Variants that cannot run in
  the current interpreter are skipped; run the script in both venvs, then `--summarize` merges the two JSON files.

"decode into a preallocated destination" is how a real capture path would avoid the intermediate ndarray. No camera is
used here: cv2.VideoCapture over an MJPEG AVI (CAP_FFMPEG) is the real VideoCapture.retrieve(image=...) API (in-place
write verified per process via np.shares_memory + pointer), and simplejpeg's buffer= is libjpeg-turbo decoding in place.
JPEG content: baseline synthetic_frames(noise=8) encoded with cv2.imencode q90, 30 distinct frames cycled (same as the
baseline e2e FakeCapture). SeqRing (proto_common.py) slots = same count as SkellyCam's 1 GiB ring (388 / 172), prefaulted.

Run (from C:\\Users\\Dom\\GitHub\\freemocap\\skellycam):
  .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe benchmarks\\frame_pipeline\\prototypes\\p1_write_variants.py
  benchmarks\\frame_pipeline\\.venv-bench\\Scripts\\python.exe benchmarks\\frame_pipeline\\prototypes\\p1_write_variants.py
  .venv\\Scripts\\python.exe benchmarks\\frame_pipeline\\prototypes\\p1_write_variants.py --summarize
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import multiprocessing as mp
import multiprocessing.queues  # noqa: F401  (skellycam type_overloads.py L23 workaround, see baseline README)
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import numpy as np  # noqa: E402

N_CAMS = 5
RUN_S = float(os.environ.get("P1_RUN_S", "10"))
WARM_S = 2.0
ONE_GIB = 1024 ** 3


def have_skellycam():
    try:
        import skellycam  # noqa: F401
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def have_simplejpeg():
    try:
        import simplejpeg  # noqa: F401
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


VARIANTS = [
    ("cur_imdecode_putframe", "S"), ("cur_memcpy_putframe", "S"), ("cur_vcap_putframe", "S"),
    ("p_imdecode_copyslot", ""), ("p_memcpy_slot", ""), ("p_vcap_into_slot", ""), ("p_simplejpeg_into_slot", "B"),
]
COPIES_AFTER_DECODE = {"cur_imdecode_putframe": 3, "cur_memcpy_putframe": 3, "cur_vcap_putframe": 2,
                       "p_imdecode_copyslot": 1, "p_memcpy_slot": 1, "p_vcap_into_slot": 0, "p_simplejpeg_into_slot": 0}
COPY_NOTE = {"cur_memcpy_putframe": "stand-in memcpy into private + copy.copy + slot",
             "p_memcpy_slot": "the stand-in memcpy goes straight into the slot"}


def make_mjpeg_avi(path: Path, jpegs, h, w, n_frames=300):
    import av
    c = av.open(str(path), "w", format="avi")
    st = c.add_stream("mjpeg", rate=60)
    st.width, st.height = w, h
    st.pix_fmt = "yuvj420p"
    for i in range(n_frames):
        pkt = av.Packet(bytes(jpegs[i % len(jpegs)]))
        pkt.stream = st
        pkt.pts = pkt.dts = i
        pkt.time_base = st.time_base
        c.mux(pkt)
    c.close()


def writer(variant, cam, h, w, spec, dto, avi_path, ready_q, start_evt, result_q):
    import cv2
    import proto_common as pcm
    cv2.setNumThreads(1)  # one camera process = one core's worth of decode, like a per-camera worker
    frames = pcm.synthetic_frames(h, w, n=30, seed=cam, noise=8)
    jpegs = [cv2.imencode(".jpg", f, [int(cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY), 90])[1] for f in frames]
    jbytes = [j.tobytes() for j in jpegs]
    pc = time.perf_counter_ns
    shape = (h, w, 3)
    info = {}
    ring = None
    sk = None
    if variant.startswith("cur_"):
        import bench_common as bc
        from skellycam.core.ipc.shared_memory.camera_shared_memory_ring_buffer import CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer
        sk = CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer.recreate(dto=dto, read_only=False)
        fr = bc.make_frame_recarray(bc.make_config(cam, h, w))
        priv = fr.image[0]
    else:
        ring = pcm.SeqRing.attach(spec)
    cap = None
    if "vcap" in variant:
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(avi_path), cv2.CAP_FFMPEG)
        info["vcap_backend"] = cap.getBackendName()
    if variant == "p_simplejpeg_into_slot":
        import simplejpeg
    k = 0

    def one():
        nonlocal k
        t0 = pc()
        j = k % 30
        if variant == "cur_imdecode_putframe":
            np.copyto(priv, cv2.imdecode(jpegs[j], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)); t1 = pc()
            fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = k
            sk.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)
        elif variant == "cur_memcpy_putframe":
            np.copyto(priv, frames[j]); t1 = pc()
            fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = k
            sk.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)
        elif variant == "cur_vcap_putframe":
            if not cap.grab():
                cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, 0); cap.grab()
            cap.retrieve(image=priv); t1 = pc()
            fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = k
            sk.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)
        else:
            s = ring.begin(k)
            view = ring.image_view(s, shape)
            if variant == "p_imdecode_copyslot":
                np.copyto(view, cv2.imdecode(jpegs[j], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR))
            elif variant == "p_memcpy_slot":
                np.copyto(view, frames[j])
            elif variant == "p_vcap_into_slot":
                if not cap.grab():
                    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, 0); cap.grab()
                cap.retrieve(image=view)
            elif variant == "p_simplejpeg_into_slot":
                simplejpeg.decode_jpeg(jbytes[j], colorspace="BGR", buffer=view)
            t1 = pc()
            ring.commit(k, s, frame_number=k, tick_ns=t0)
        t2 = pc()
        k += 1
        return t0, t1, t2

    # in-place verification for the zero-copy variants
    if variant == "p_vcap_into_slot":
        s = 0; view = ring.image_view(s, shape); view[:] = 0
        cap.grab(); ok, out = cap.retrieve(image=view)
        info["inplace_verified"] = bool(out is not None and np.shares_memory(out, view)
                                        and out.__array_interface__["data"][0] == view.__array_interface__["data"][0]
                                        and int(view.sum(dtype=np.int64)) > 0)
    if variant == "p_simplejpeg_into_slot":
        s = 0; view = ring.image_view(s, shape); view[:] = 0
        out = simplejpeg.decode_jpeg(jbytes[0], colorspace="BGR", buffer=view)
        ref = cv2.imdecode(jpegs[0], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        info["inplace_verified"] = bool(np.shares_memory(out, view) and int(view.sum(dtype=np.int64)) > 0)
        info["max_abs_diff_vs_cv2_imdecode"] = int(np.abs(view.astype(np.int16) - ref.astype(np.int16)).max())
    # warm-up: one full ring lap (first-touch) + WARM_S
    L = sk.ring_buffer_length if sk is not None else ring.L
    for _ in range(L):
        one()
    tw = pc() + int(WARM_S * 1e9)
    while pc() < tw:
        one()
    ready_q.put(cam)
    start_evt.wait()
    dec, pub, tot = [], [], []
    cpu0 = time.process_time()
    t_start = pc()
    deadline = t_start + int(RUN_S * 1e9)
    while True:
        t0, t1, t2 = one()
        dec.append(t1 - t0); pub.append(t2 - t1); tot.append(t2 - t0)
        if t2 >= deadline:
            break
    el = (pc() - t_start) / 1e9
    cpu = time.process_time() - cpu0
    n = len(tot)
    if cap is not None:
        cap.release()
    result_q.put(dict(cam=cam, n=n, elapsed_s=el, fps=n / el, cpu_ms_per_frame=1000 * cpu / n,
                      cpu_pct=100 * cpu / el, decode_or_capture=pcm.stats_ms(dec), publish=pcm.stats_ms(pub),
                      total=pcm.stats_ms(tot), ring_len=L, **info))
    if sk is not None:
        sk.close()
    else:
        ring.close()


def run(variant, size_name):
    import cv2
    import proto_common as pcm
    h, w = pcm.SIZES[size_name]
    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
    ring = None
    skshm = None
    dtos = {}
    specs = {}
    rings = []
    if variant.startswith("cur_"):
        import bench_common as bc
        from skellycam.core.ipc.shared_memory.camera_group_shared_memory import CameraGroupSharedMemory
        from skellycam.core.timestamps.timebase_mapping import TimebaseMapping
        configs = {str(i): bc.make_config(i, h, w) for i in range(N_CAMS)}
        skshm = CameraGroupSharedMemory.create(camera_configs=configs, timebase_mapping=TimebaseMapping(), read_only=True)
        dtos = skshm.camera_shm_dtos
    else:
        rec_bytes = 632 + h * w * 3  # same per-slot budget as a SkellyCam record -> same slot count for 1 GiB
        L = ONE_GIB // rec_bytes
        for i in range(N_CAMS):
            r = pcm.SeqRing.create(L, h * w * 3, prefault=True)
            rings.append(r)
            specs[str(i)] = r.spec()
    avi = {}
    if "vcap" in variant:
        for i in range(N_CAMS):
            frames = pcm.synthetic_frames(h, w, n=30, seed=i, noise=8)
            jpegs = [cv2.imencode(".jpg", f, [int(cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY), 90])[1] for f in frames]
            p = pcm.SCRATCH_TMP / f"p1_{size_name}_cam{i}.avi"
            make_mjpeg_avi(p, jpegs, h, w)
            avi[str(i)] = p
    ready_q, result_q, start_evt = ctx.Queue(), ctx.Queue(), ctx.Event()
    procs = [ctx.Process(target=writer, args=(variant, i, h, w, specs.get(str(i)), dtos.get(str(i)), avi.get(str(i)),
                                              ready_q, start_evt, result_q)) for i in range(N_CAMS)]
    for p in procs:
        p.start()
    for _ in procs:
        ready_q.get(timeout=300)
    start_evt.set()
    res = sorted([result_q.get(timeout=300) for _ in procs], key=lambda r: r["cam"])
    for p in procs:
        p.join(30)
    if skshm is not None:
        skshm.unlink_and_close()
    for r in rings:
        r.close()
    avi_bytes = {k: v.stat().st_size for k, v in avi.items()}
    for v in avi.values():
        v.unlink()
    fb = h * w * 3
    agg = sum(r["fps"] for r in res)
    return dict(variant=variant, size=size_name, n_cams=N_CAMS, run_s=RUN_S, per_camera=res,
                min_cam_fps=min(r["fps"] for r in res), aggregate_fps=agg, aggregate_GBps_frames=agg * fb / 1e9,
                median_total_ms=float(np.median([r["total"]["median_ms"] for r in res])),
                worst_p99_total_ms=max(r["total"]["p99_ms"] for r in res),
                median_decode_ms=float(np.median([r["decode_or_capture"]["median_ms"] for r in res])),
                median_publish_ms=float(np.median([r["publish"]["median_ms"] for r in res])),
                worst_p99_publish_ms=max(r["publish"]["p99_ms"] for r in res),
                cpu_ms_per_frame=float(np.median([r["cpu_ms_per_frame"] for r in res])),
                full_frame_copies_after_decode=COPIES_AFTER_DECODE[variant], copy_note=COPY_NOTE.get(variant, ""),
                avi_bytes=avi_bytes, inplace_verified=[r.get("inplace_verified") for r in res])


def summarize():
    import json
    import proto_common as pcm
    rows = []
    envs = {}
    for tag in ("skellycamvenv", "benchvenv"):
        p = pcm.RESULTS / f"p1_write_{tag}.json"
        if p.exists():
            d = json.loads(p.read_text())
            envs[tag] = {k: d["env"].get(k) for k in ("time", "system_cpu_pct_1s_before_run", "executable", "simplejpeg")}
            rows += [dict(r, venv=tag) for r in d["rows"]]
    order = [v for v, _ in VARIANTS]
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["size"], order.index(r["variant"])))
    L = ["# P1 - camera write path: decode/capture + publish into shm (5 spawned processes, unthrottled)",
         "", f"RUN_S={RUN_S}s per config after 1 ring lap + {WARM_S}s warm-up; cv2.setNumThreads(1) per process; 30 distinct q90 JPEGs.",
         "`total` = decode/capture + publish per frame. `publish` = everything after the pixels exist (put_frame, or seq commit).",
         "", "| size | variant | venv | per-cam fps (min) | total median / worst p99 ms | decode/capture median ms | publish median / worst p99 ms | CPU ms/frame | full-frame copies after decode | in-place verified |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rows:
        L.append(f"| {r['size']} | {r['variant']} | {r['venv']} | {r['min_cam_fps']:.0f} | {r['median_total_ms']:.3f} / {r['worst_p99_total_ms']:.3f} | "
                 f"{r['median_decode_ms']:.3f} | {r['median_publish_ms']:.3f} / {r['worst_p99_publish_ms']:.3f} | {r['cpu_ms_per_frame']:.3f} | "
                 f"{r['full_frame_copies_after_decode']} | {r['inplace_verified'] if any(v is not None for v in r['inplace_verified']) else '-'} |")
    L += ["", "Environment (per run): " + json.dumps(envs)]
    pcm.write_text("p1_write.md", "\n".join(L) + "\n")
    print("\n".join(L))


def main():
    import proto_common as pcm
    if "--summarize" in sys.argv:
        summarize(); return
    sk, sj = have_skellycam(), have_simplejpeg()
    tag = "skellycamvenv" if sk else "benchvenv"
    sel = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    out = {"env": pcm.env_summary(), "run_s": RUN_S, "rows": []}
    for size_name in ("720p", "1080p"):
        for v, need in VARIANTS:
            if sel and v not in sel:
                continue
            if (need == "S" and not sk) or (need == "B" and not sj):
                continue
            if tag == "benchvenv" and need == "" and v != "p_imdecode_copyslot":
                continue  # the venv-independent variants run once (skellycam venv) + one cross-check row here
            r = run(v, size_name)
            out["rows"].append(r)
            pcm.write_json(f"p1_write_{tag}.json", out)
            print(f"{size_name} {v}: min fps {r['min_cam_fps']:.0f}, total {r['median_total_ms']:.3f}/{r['worst_p99_total_ms']:.3f} ms, "
                  f"decode {r['median_decode_ms']:.3f}, publish {r['median_publish_ms']:.3f}/{r['worst_p99_publish_ms']:.3f}, "
                  f"cpu {r['cpu_ms_per_frame']:.3f} ms/f, inplace {r['inplace_verified']}", flush=True)
    sys.stdout.flush()
    os._exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    st.width, st.height = w, h
    st.pix_fmt = "yuvj420p"
    for i in range(n_frames):
        pkt = av.Packet(bytes(jpegs[i % len(jpegs)]))
        pkt.stream = st
        pkt.pts = pkt.dts = i
        pkt.time_base = st.time_base
        c.mux(pkt)
    c.close()


def writer(variant, cam, h, w, spec, dto, avi_path, ready_q, start_evt, result_q):
    import cv2
    import proto_common as pcm
    cv2.setNumThreads(1)  # one camera process = one core's worth of decode, like a per-camera worker
    frames = pcm.synthetic_frames(h, w, n=30, seed=cam, noise=8)
    jpegs = [cv2.imencode(".jpg", f, [int(cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY), 90])[1] for f in frames]
    jbytes = [j.tobytes() for j in jpegs]
    pc = time.perf_counter_ns
    shape = (h, w, 3)
    info = {}
    ring = None
    sk = None
    if variant.startswith("cur_"):
        import bench_common as bc
        from skellycam.core.ipc.shared_memory.camera_shared_memory_ring_buffer import CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer
        sk = CameraSharedMemoryRingBuffer.recreate(dto=dto, read_only=False)
        fr = bc.make_frame_recarray(bc.make_config(cam, h, w))
        priv = fr.image[0]
    else:
        ring = pcm.SeqRing.attach(spec)
    cap = None
    if "vcap" in variant:
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(avi_path), cv2.CAP_FFMPEG)
        info["vcap_backend"] = cap.getBackendName()
    if variant == "p_simplejpeg_into_slot":
        import simplejpeg
    k = 0

    def one():
        nonlocal k
        t0 = pc()
        j = k % 30
        if variant == "cur_imdecode_putframe":
            np.copyto(priv, cv2.imdecode(jpegs[j], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)); t1 = pc()
            fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = k
            sk.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)
        elif variant == "cur_memcpy_putframe":
            np.copyto(priv, frames[j]); t1 = pc()
            fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = k
            sk.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)
        elif variant == "cur_vcap_putframe":
            if not cap.grab():
                cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, 0); cap.grab()
            cap.retrieve(image=priv); t1 = pc()
            fr.frame_metadata.frame_number[0] = k
            sk.put_frame(frame_rec_array=fr, overwrite=True)
        else:
            s = ring.begin(k)
            view = ring.image_view(s, shape)
            if variant == "p_imdecode_copyslot":
                np.copyto(view, cv2.imdecode(jpegs[j], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR))
            elif variant == "p_memcpy_slot":
                np.copyto(view, frames[j])
            elif variant == "p_vcap_into_slot":
                if not cap.grab():
                    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, 0); cap.grab()
                cap.retrieve(image=view)
            elif variant == "p_simplejpeg_into_slot":
                simplejpeg.decode_jpeg(jbytes[j], colorspace="BGR", buffer=view)
            t1 = pc()
            ring.commit(k, s, frame_number=k, tick_ns=t0)
        t2 = pc()
        k += 1
        return t0, t1, t2

    # in-place verification for the zero-copy variants
    if variant == "p_vcap_into_slot":
        s = 0; view = ring.image_view(s, shape); view[:] = 0
        cap.grab(); ok, out = cap.retrieve(image=view)
        info["inplace_verified"] = bool(out is not None and np.shares_memory(out, view)
                                        and out.__array_interface__["data"][0] == view.__array_interface__["data"][0]
                                        and int(view.sum(dtype=np.int64)) > 0)
    if variant == "p_simplejpeg_into_slot":
        s = 0; view = ring.image_view(s, shape); view[:] = 0
        out = simplejpeg.decode_jpeg(jbytes[0], colorspace="BGR", buffer=view)
        ref = cv2.imdecode(jpegs[0], cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        info["inplace_verified"] = bool(np.shares_memory(out, view) and int(view.sum(dtype=np.int64)) > 0)
        info["max_abs_diff_vs_cv2_imdecode"] = int(np.abs(view.astype(np.int16) - ref.astype(np.int16)).max())
    # warm-up: one full ring lap (first-touch) + WARM_S
    L = sk.ring_buffer_length if sk is not None else ring.L
    for _ in range(L):
        one()
    tw = pc() + int(WARM_S * 1e9)
    while pc() < tw:
        one()
    ready_q.put(cam)
    start_evt.wait()
    dec, pub, tot = [], [], []
    cpu0 = time.process_time()
    t_start = pc()
    deadline = t_start + int(RUN_S * 1e9)
    while True:
        t0, t1, t2 = one()
        dec.append(t1 - t0); pub.append(t2 - t1); tot.append(t2 - t0)
        if t2 >= deadline:
            break
    el = (pc() - t_start) / 1e9
    cpu = time.process_time() - cpu0
    n = len(tot)
    if cap is not None:
        cap.release()
    result_q.put(dict(cam=cam, n=n, elapsed_s=el, fps=n / el, cpu_ms_per_frame=1000 * cpu / n,
                      cpu_pct=100 * cpu / el, decode_or_capture=pcm.stats_ms(dec), publish=pcm.stats_ms(pub),
                      total=pcm.stats_ms(tot), ring_len=L, **info))
    if sk is not None:
        sk.close()
    else:
        ring.close()

    import proto_common as pcm
    h, w = pcm.SIZES[size_name]
    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
    ring = None
    skshm = None
    dtos = {}
    specs = {}
    rings = []

        from skellycam.core.ipc.shared_memory.camera_group_shared_memory import CameraGroupSharedMemory
        from skellycam.core.timestamps.timebase_mapping import TimebaseMapping
        configs = {str(i): bc.make_config(i, h, w) for i in range(N_CAMS)}
        skshm = CameraGroupSharedMemory.create(camera_configs=configs, timebase_mapping=TimebaseMapping(), read_only=True)
        dtos = skshm.camera_shm_dtos
    else:
        rec_bytes = 632 + h * w * 3  # same per-slot budget as a SkellyCam record -> same slot count for 1 GiB
        L = ONE_GIB // rec_bytes
        for i in range(N_CAMS):

            rings.append(r)
            specs[str(i)] = r.spec()
    avi = {}
    if "vcap" in variant:
        for i in range(N_CAMS):

            jpegs = [cv2.imencode(".jpg", f, [int(cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY), 90])[1] for f in frames]
            p = pcm.SCRATCH_TMP / f"p1_{size_name}_cam{i}.avi"

    for p in procs:

    for _ in procs:

    start_evt.set()
    res = sorted([result_q.get(timeout=300) for _ in procs], key=lambda r: r["cam"])

    if skshm is not None:
        skshm.unlink_and_close()

                min_cam_fps=min(r["fps"] for r in res), aggregate_fps=agg, aggregate_GBps_frames=agg * fb / 1e9,
                median_total_ms=float(np.median([r["total"]["median_ms"] for r in res])),
                worst_p99_total_ms=max(r["total"]["p99_ms"] for r in res),
                median_decode_ms=float(np.median([r["decode_or_capture"]["median_ms"] for r in res])),
                median_publish_ms=float(np.median([r["publish"]["median_ms"] for r in res])),
                worst_p99_publish_ms=max(r["publish"]["p99_ms"] for r in res),
                cpu_ms_per_frame=float(np.median([r["cpu_ms_per_frame"] for r in res])),
                full_frame_copies_after_decode=COPIES_AFTER_DECODE[variant], copy_note=COPY_NOTE.get(variant, ""),
                avi_bytes=avi_bytes, inplace_verified=[r.get("inplace_verified") for r in res])

    import json
    import proto_common as pcm
    rows = []
    envs = {}
    for tag in ("skellycamvenv", "benchvenv"):
        p = pcm.RESULTS / f"p1_write_{tag}.json"
        if p.exists():
            d = json.loads(p.read_text())
            envs[tag] = {k: d["env"].get(k) for k in ("time", "system_cpu_pct_1s_before_run", "executable", "simplejpeg")}

         "", f"RUN_S={RUN_S}s per config after 1 ring lap + {WARM_S}s warm-up; cv2.setNumThreads(1) per process; 30 distinct q90 JPEGs.",
         "`total` = decode/capture + publish per frame. `publish` = everything after the pixels exist (put_frame, or seq commit).",
         "", "| size | variant | venv | per-cam fps (min) | total median / worst p99 ms | decode/capture median ms | publish median / worst p99 ms | CPU ms/frame | full-frame copies after decode | in-place verified |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for r in rows:
        L.append(f"| {r['size']} | {r['variant']} | {r['venv']} | {r['min_cam_fps']:.0f} | {r['median_total_ms']:.3f} / {r['worst_p99_total_ms']:.3f} | "
                 f"{r['median_decode_ms']:.3f} | {r['median_publish_ms']:.3f} / {r['worst_p99_publish_ms']:.3f} | {r['cpu_ms_per_frame']:.3f} | "
                 f"{r['full_frame_copies_after_decode']} | {r['inplace_verified'] if any(v is not None for v in r['inplace_verified']) else '-'} |")
